Art helps us feel, understand, and connect.

Artbitrage takes the shape of many rooms because looking, reading, listening, and playing can each open something different. There is no right order, and no need to see it all.

Find a particular room ↓

A few ways to begin.

Choose a path for today, or make your own. Each room is a place you can stay, leave, and return to.

01 Look closer

Meet a work. Follow the feeling.

Begin with what a painting brings up for you, then explore the lives and materials behind it. Let a poem offer another way of seeing.

  1. What caught my eyeFollow five artworks through personal notes and small details.↗
  2. The DepthsExplore a work through feeling, making, and history.↗
  3. The Answering RhymesRead poems alongside paintings, across cultures.↗

02 Take your time

Let your eye lead.

Spend a while with pictures. Pause with any work during the gallery visit, or settle into the quiet room for a longer stay. There is no pace to keep.

  1. 五行 · Five ways of lookingFollow wood, fire, earth, metal and water through art.↗
  2. The RiverChoose a current and move through artworks.↗
  3. Good Trip · the quiet roomStay with a picture, follow a breath, or find an anchor. Sound if you choose.↗

03 Follow a life

Find the people and places.

Art belongs to a world. Meet the people, materials and knowledge behind it, then find the places where works live and the care that keeps them with us.

  1. Behind the workFollow the craft, materials and continuing care of art.↗
  2. 無名 · UnsignedMeet ten works whose makers the museum record does not name.↗
  3. The MindsDiscover artists, their ideas, and their ways of looking.↗
  4. The AtlasLocate works and imagine a visit in person.↗

04 Stay curious

Make room for play.

Follow the project's more personal paths into manga, imagination, and language play. These rooms share the interests and associations behind this place.

  1. NenA playful reading of art through Hunter × Hunter.↗
  2. HomecomingA personal wordplay project around Cantonese tones.↗

The images are details. Tap an artwork to spend a moment with the whole piece. Images courtesy of the Art Institute of Chicago, CC0; each caption links to its museum record.
